question: Which native server process owns admitted work, and which independently identified sessions share its failure domain?

deployment.DSH: dsh web: loopback, shipped Web composition, fresh owned DSH_HOME, public authenticated session create/prompt/wait API
deployment.OpenClaw: gateway run: loopback, fresh owned state, public authenticated OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint

scope: Platform uses long-lived native servers. Earlier Harness CTX studies used per-invocation headless/embedded entries; their resource points do not stand in for service ownership or warm/idle platform cost.

calibration.provider: deterministic independent local HTTP service; synthetic usage, no paid credentials
assertions: Distinct actual native session identities sharing one service/state root
Each random user marker reaches actual provider request
Native terminal output contains fixture-only acknowledgment
Sanitized launch logs and process ancestry retained

future_fault_conditions: abrupt client exit at independently observed admitted provider boundary
fidelity_requirements: Freeze actual client and service owner PIDs using process/cgroup witnesses; never infer owner from wrapper Popen PID
SIGTERM may send native cancellation, so cannot stand in for abrupt client loss without a distinct label
Keep same native server deployment, principal and session topology within each product block
Observe companion terminal outcome, native persisted state and recovery rather than treating a disconnected response as task failure
Freeze full fault/recovery/no-progress protocol and pilot-derived whole-block estimate before formal two-block admission
Blind native-log reconstruction remains required by PA; external truth may not earn native observability credit
